script.text: Chip stocks just fell eight days in a row. Is the AI boom cracking?

On Friday the Nasdaq fell 2.1 percent to 26,140, its worst week since June, CNBC reports. The Philadelphia chip index lost 3.8 percent. That was its eighth straight daily drop, the longest streak since 2008, Investing.com says.

CNBC ties the sell-off to doubts about AI spending and to high oil prices. Market reports say Brent crude settled near 110 dollars, the highest since May. The Wall Street Journal adds worries about Chinese memory chip makers.

Micron fell 5.6 percent and Intel 5.8 percent, market reports say. The chip index now sits 23.9 percent below its June record. The S and P 500 closed down 1.1 percent at 7,659. The Dow slipped 0.3 percent to 52,002.
Will chip stocks stop falling this week? Yes or no?
